muc.title: Numbers ready, slides needed
muc.text: The numbers are ready, and now Mark's aunt needs five slides for the start-of-month staff meeting. In this last part, Claude builds the deck from the Excel results of part 2, and this is a real PowerPoint file it made.

muc.title: The same add-in
muc.text: In PowerPoint, the add-in is part of the same Claude for Microsoft 365 package installed in part 2: go to Home, Add-ins and click Claude. Pick a slide template first, because Claude reads the slide master, the deck's layout template, to use the right fonts and colors.

muc.title: Numbers straight from Excel
muc.text: Ask Claude to use the results in the open Excel file to build five slides: overview, items going up, items going down, peak hours and recommendations. Every number on the slides comes straight from the summary table, with nothing retyped.

muc.title: Click to edit
muc.text: The charts in the slides are real PowerPoint charts you can click to edit the numbers, not pasted images. The peak-hours slide shows that 5 pm to 8 pm brings in 42 percent of revenue.

muc.title: Only that slide changes
muc.text: Slide 3 has five long lines, so ask for it to be cut to three, and only that slide changes while the others stay the same.

muc.title: Bullets into a diagram
muc.text: The recommendations slide is three bullet points, so ask Claude to turn it into a three-step process diagram, move it to the front and add a contents slide for the whole deck.

muc.title: Check every number
muc.text: The draft comes out fast, but you still check every number against the Excel file before presenting. Habits like one line per bullet go into the Instructions box once.

muc.title: Your wordiest slide
muc.text: Open an old presentation, pick the slide with the most text, and ask Claude to turn it into a diagram or chart.

muc.title: Three places to work
muc.text: So there are three places to work: Chrome for web tasks, Excel for numbers, PowerPoint for slides. All three need a paid plan, Pro or higher, and you're always the one who does the final check.
